brief: Elon Musk said over the weekend that Tesla/SpaceX are in discussions with TSMC for US semiconductor capacity, following last week's report that TSMC is weighing a second US fab cluster in Texas. JPM's supply-chain checks indicate early talks are aimed at a pure-foundry or JV structure (similar to JSMC/ESMC), giving Tesla/SpaceX a dedicated capacity corridor; the fab would ramp in 2030 and beyond, with the first three phases of TSMC's US expansion still centered on Arizona. JPM expects TSMC to keep process/technology control and majority fab ownership, unlike Intel's Tesla TeraFab 14A agreement. The driver cited is strong compute demand (SpaceX reportedly selling compute at $20-30 per watt) plus signs of slower competitor process ramps (Tesla AI6 possibly re-engaging TSMC; new ASIC programs with MediaTek going to TSMC, not Intel). JPM reads this as diminishing TSMC's competitive-threat narrative, supporting its PE multiple, and reiterates Overweight with a NT$3300 price target (20x 12-month forward EPS). A Tesla switch-back to TSMC could also benefit GUC, Tesla's AI5 design partner, which had faced AI6 share-loss risk.
